subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Unit 3 – Lesson 5: Culture (traditional sports in Oman)
outcomes: I can name two traditional sports in Oman.
I can say facts about camel racing and dhow racing.
I can write about a favourite sport: … likes … He plays … on …

tf.s: Camel racing is a traditional sport in Oman.
tf.why: Yes! Camel racing is a traditional Omani sport.

tf.s: Camel racing is a new sport in Oman.
tf.why: Camel racing is a traditional sport, not a new one.

tf.s: A dhow is a traditional sailing boat.
tf.why: Right! A dhow is a traditional sailing boat.

tf.s: A dhow is a traditional house.
tf.why: A dhow is a boat, not a house.

tf.s: Camels can run at about 64 kilometres an hour.
Camels can run at about 6 kilometres an hour.
tf.why: Camels can run at about 64 kilometres an hour.

tf.s: Dhow racing is a traditional sport in Oman.
tf.why: Yes! Camel racing and dhow racing are traditional sports.

tf.s: A tennis player has got a racket and tennis balls.
tf.why: Yes! He's got a racket and tennis balls.

mcq.q: Maryam likes basketball. She plays on Mondays. Choose the page sentences.
o: Maryam likes basketball. She plays basketball on Mondays.
Maryam like basketball. She play basketball on Mondays.
Maryam likes basketball. She plays basketball at Mondays.

mcq.q: Riddle: He's got a racket and a ball. What sport is it?
mcq.why: A racket and ball are for tennis.

mcq.why: 64 km an hour is very fast!

mcq.why: A dhow is a sailing boat, so dhow racing uses one.
